subject: Vendor replacement evaluation — compatibility, onboarding credit & price-hold
messages:
From: James Park <j.park@horizon.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor replacement: confirmation of platform fit & pricing ask

Stephanie —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. We are moving forward with an internal vendor replacement evaluation and Redwood is on the shortlist. Before we commit a cross-functional team, procurement asked for two things we hope you can confirm quickly:

1) Can Redwood provide a short-term price-match (unit pricing + egress structure) that we can hold for 30 days while we finalize legal? We anticipate a 12-month committed consumption profile with monthly spikes (peak 3x baseline for product launches).

2) Is Redwood willing to provide an onboarding credit to offset integration work (data egress, connector builds, and a short pilot)? We need both the financial ask and a high-level timeline for switching (minimal downtime is a hard requirement).

Attached is a light SOW and our expected traffic profile.

Attachments: [Attachment: Horizon_SOW_outline.pdf (PDF, 420 KB)]

Best,
James Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Horizon Cloud
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: James Park <j.park@horizon.ai>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor replacement: confirmation of platform fit & pricing ask

Thanks James — appreciate the concise note and the SOW.

Short answers up-front:
- Price-hold: Yes, we can hold a matched unit price for 30 days pending a signed commitment and scope confirmation for a 12-month term.
- Onboarding credit: Yes — we can extend a one-time onboarding package (credits + 40 engineering hours of onboarding support) contingent on a minimum commit.

Next steps I propose:
1) Connor, can you validate the technical fit and confirm any integration caveats (KV cache warmup, model variants, egress behavior)? Please include a 3-week pilot plan and estimated SE hours.
2) Marissa, I’ll loop you into pricing cadence — we should produce a compact commercial summary (price-hold + credit schedule + DocuSign link) by EOD tomorrow.
3) James, once you confirm stake-holders and the expected signature date, we’ll lock the timeline.

I’ve attached a quick estimate workbook we use for onboarding planning — Connor, feel free to update.

Attachments: [Attachment: RI_onboard_estimate.xlsx (Excel, 45 KB)]

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Vendor replacement: confirmation of platform fit & pricing ask

Stephanie / Marissa —

Quick technical summary after a light read of Horizon_SOW_outline.pdf and the traffic profile James shared:

High-level compatibility notes:
- Model runtime: Horizon uses a mix of decoder-only generation with peaky traffic (short bursts for inference). Redwood’s serving runtime supports the same model families and can run the variants you listed with no model-rewrite.
- KV/prefix caching: We recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for the initial ramp — reduces token cost by ~35% for Horizon’s usage pattern and helps with latency during spikes.
- Onboarding window: 3–5 business days for a staged pilot (sandbox -> dedicated pilot). Full cutover with validation and runbook handoff: ~2–3 weeks depending on feature gating and connectors.

Estimated resource needs (ballpark):
- SE effort: 40–60 hours (pilot + connector testing + runbook)
- Infra ops: small dedicated pool for first 30 days to absorb burst traffic (can be scheduled as burst capacity — see notes in the attached workbook)
- Risk: Egress verification and long-tail tokenization corner-cases (we’ll validate on the pilot).

Pricing implications: enabling prefix caching + short dedicated buffer reduces per-token spend materially; we can model three scenarios in the commercial summary (baseline, burst-enabled, and optimized-cache).

Related internal link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/horizon-onboard-prototype (internal benchmarking notes)

Attachments I’ll provide to pricing: updated RI_onboard_estimate.xlsx with SE-hour breakdown and a short pilot checklist.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: James Park <j.park@horizon.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood offer: 30-day price-hold + onboarding credit (commercial summary)

James —

Per our thread and Connor’s technical read, attached is a short commercial summary that captures:

- Price-hold: Redwood will match the unit rates provided in your SOW for an identical billing cadence and egress assumptions. This price-hold is valid for 30 calendar days from the DocuSign signature request date.
- Commit: 12-month minimum committed spend (details in the attached commercial summary).
- Onboarding credit: $45,000 equivalent in credits plus 40 SE hours of onboarding support (applied as a one-time credit on first invoice).
- Pilot plan: 3-week staged pilot with a dedicated buffer for launch day spikes.
- Fallbacks: We will configure automatic model-variant fallback and region routing to keep latency SLOs during heavy bursts.

To lock the price-hold we’ll need:
1) Signed commercial summary (DocuSign link below)
2) Confirmation of primary technical contacts and proposed signature date

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/DocuSignLink/example-8921

If you’d like, we can also include a 60-day runway on the onboarding credit at a small increase to the committed spend; happy to run that alternative.

Please let me know a target for signature and any final procurement paperwork. If you’re ready I can request the DocuSign today and mark the price-hold start date.

Best,

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
